title: Support inline tooltips in Markdown (hover text), e.g. via a `:tooltip[...]` directive
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a way to include inline text in Markdown that shows a tooltip when hovered — like abbreviations/glossary terms with an explanation on hover. This could be exposed as a new Markdown directive, and #12474 (show footnotes as tooltips) could be generalized to cover this.

### Why?

It's common to want to annotate a word or phrase with extra context that appears on hover — glossary terms, acronym expansions, definitions, or short explanations — without cluttering the main text. Today there's no native way to do this in Streamlit Markdown; users resort to raw HTML (`<abbr>`/`title`) which is limited and not always allowed. A first-class inline tooltip makes docs, dashboards, and explanatory text much richer.

### How?

Add a Markdown directive for inline tooltips, where the bracketed text is displayed and the `text` attribute is shown on hover:

```
The :tooltip[HTML]{text="Hyper Text Markup Language"} specification...

:tooltip[Streamlit]{text="Open-source app framework for Machine Learning and Data Science teams."}
```

Notes:
- The visible text (`[...]`) renders inline; hovering shows the tooltip `text`.
- Works wherever Streamlit Markdown is rendered (`st.markdown`, `st.write`, captions, etc.).
- Consider whether the tooltip `text` itself supports Markdown.
- **Alternative / complementary:** generalize #12474 (footnotes → tooltips). Markdown footnotes could render as hover tooltips, giving a standard-Markdown path to the same result; the `:tooltip[...]` directive is the more explicit, inline alternative.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12474 (show markdown footnotes as tooltips) — this issue proposes a more generic, directive-based approach to inline hover text.
